evidence.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.001, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8
This card has 9 earlier purchases billed to region 485 (first on 2016-07-10)

The alert's score (0.71, as in the case record) differs from the score stored on the transaction (0.07). Two bank sources disagree, and neither moves the decision: the bank warns its model is near useless for January, so its score is not used as evidence

case.summary: This alert was triggered because the bank's real-time risk score flagged transaction 3601725 for $112.75 on card C00543-K1. Graph and historical evidence showed that the transaction amount is typical for this card and the customer has a history of purchases in the same billing region. Additionally, the transaction model scored the event very low, indicating minimal risk based on unnamed model features and past account behavior. The verdict is legitimate, and the final actions are to allow the transaction and close the case with no fraud.
